## Verdict: FAIL — line B-SIMPLE CONFIRMED on its class (row 127's networks simple and clear of way:0's band, committed as read; census never rising; smoke clean; NEAR green), but NOT closed: the round's guard `RING_CROSSES` refuses LAWFUL input that round S15 committed (a face holding a dangling chain of two or more edges — kerb, corridorUnion and bandUnion), and four of this seat's mutants on the guard and the faithful read's acceptance survive the item's whole test set non-equivalently (MG1, MG3, MA2, MQ2)

The fix itself does what row 128 asked on its class (section (1)): on the three row-127 networks every face's kerb(F) is
simple, way:0's deepest vertex 25.95 cm, the committed blocks the read (round S15's engine reproduces P127: face 0 not
simple, 33.97 cm); 177 further variants of the network read simple with no refusal (round S15's engine: 6 not simple);
the sampling oracle finds every re-recorded pin closer to §3.7's F − ⋃ buffer than round S15's read; the census never
rises; the 26 smoke seeds are clean but for fusion 24 / 36 (the clause's own, as S15); NEAR, B-FUZZ at both seeds and
RELATED meet only the known foreign reds.

What fails is the round's last guard (N-45 (a)'s detect-and-refuse), which the round added beside the fix:

**B-GUARD (probes ANT and BU; notes row 142).** `ringCrosses` counts two edges "running along one another" as a
crossing, so F's own walk out and back along a dangling chain of two or more edges — a lawful L1 face, the walk
`… (2000, 0) (2000, 800) (2600, 1500) (2000, 800) (2000, 0) …` — is refused E_INVARIANT `RING_CROSSES` wherever the read
returns F's walk, i.e. wherever the face is spine-less for the read: kerb(F) and corridorUnion refuse a spine-less face
holding a widthless dangling chain (a `wall`, a `district_bound`, a way with no width; straight or bent; from the frame
or T'd off a chord), and **bandUnion refuses whole** over faces one of which holds a two-segment cul-de-sac WAY (half-width
20) that the band's read does not buffer (BU: frame, way:0 a chord at hw 30, way:1 the cul-de-sac (1000, 0) → (1000, 800)
→ (1500, 1400) at hw 20, wall:1 (3000, 2000) → (3000, 4000) banded at 50 cm square; corridorUnion commits, bandUnion
refuses `E_INVARIANT arr: a ring of the read region crosses itself (N-45)`). Round S15's engine commits every one of
them (kerb(F) = F, one whole block; bandUnion band 4 / blocks 4); a one-edge dangling chain is still accepted (its two
walk edges are neighbours). So the round raised the refusals of a lawful class from 0 (J264: a closing checker fails
the round when its refusals rise; N-58: a lawful class is never left at REFUSE), broke the item's listed clause "a face
with no bounding spine: kerb(F) = F, one built block" for such faces, and contradicts its own C-0425 / kerb.ts text
("a ring that only touches itself at a vertex (a pinch: … as a face holding a dangling chain's tip is walked) is no
crossing"). B-FUZZ cannot see it: its dead ends are one segment and every way has a width.

**Mutant survivors (section (1), notes row 143).** Of this seat's 22 targeted mutants, 15 are killed; MF3, MA4 and MR1
make 0 kerb differences in 4 618 reads (equivalent on every input met); four survive the item's two folders at
PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS=1000 and are NOT equivalent: MG1 (the guard removed) and MG3 (`ringCrosses` without its collinear-overlap
clause) differ on the 6 ANT faces — the guard has no pin on a ring that really crosses (no test reaches it; the builder's
"no reachable pin", row 138, is contradicted by ANT / BU); MA2 (the acceptance without "no vertex deeper than the first's
deepest") differs on 2 widened networks, taking a faithful read deeper than the first (26.77 → 26.84, 29.00 → 30.82 cm)
— C-0425's "no read is made worse" is unpinned (the builder's AC1, "0 differences in 5 057 reads", is contradicted);
MQ2 (`readQuality` without its junction-end reading) moves 3 chord reads (one from 17.00 to 29.64 cm deep). The brief:
a survivor on a stated promise that is not equivalent stays a blocker.

**Required change (the next a-09 round, inside the item's owns; or the session's ruling, maxRounds 1):** (a) the guard
refuses only a ring that crosses itself; F's own walk round a dangling chain — out and back along the same route edges,
a bridge or antenna of any length, as it already accepts a pinch — is no crossing, so kerb(F) = F for a spine-less face,
corridorUnion commits it whole and bandUnion commits over faces holding a cul-de-sac (MAKE-IT-SUCCEED, N-58: lawful
input; the census before / after), pinned by the ANT faces (a two-segment straight and a bent widthless chain from the
frame, one T'd off a chord; roles way-without-width, `wall`, `district_bound`) and the BU network, each red on today's
engine and green as round S15 read them; (b) the guard pinned on a ring that really crosses (e.g. round S15's row-127
outline planted through bandCore's `pieces` seam, as closing.test.ts plants), so MG1 and MG3 are killed; (c) MA2's and
MQ2's clauses pinned by the inputs notes row 143 names, or each stated in C-0425 as a heuristic with no pin and its
reason.

Also routed (not blockers; notes rows 144, 145): pre-existing depth classes within the read's declared bounds and
identical on round S15's engine — a closed ring way's seam corner kept to the centreline for half-widths 27 – 36 cm
(row 139 (b)'s class), commit-time attraction onto a crossing vertex (P127 variants: blocks up to 38.34 cm into way:0's

## (3) New findings by the blocker rule

**B-GUARD — BLOCKER (a lawful-input refusal the round introduced, J264 / N-58; the item's listed clause "a face with no
bounding spine: kerb(F) = F, one built block" broken for faces holding a dangling chain; non-equivalent surviving
mutants on the guard's stated promise).** Evidence (probes ANT, `zz-check16-ant.test.ts`, and BU,
`zz-check16-bu.test.ts`; final engine against round S15's in `s15m`):

| input (frame [0, 4000]², the faces owned by district:1) | final engine | round S15's engine |
|---|---|---|
| a one-edge widthless dangling chain (2000, 0) → (2000, 1500) | kerb ok, CU whole [0] | the same |
| a two-edge straight widthless chain (2000, 0) → (2000, 800) → (2000, 1500); roles way (no width), `wall`, `district_bound` | kerb and CU `E_INVARIANT arr: a ring of the read region crosses itself (N-45)` | kerb(F) = F's walk, CU whole [0] |
| a bent widthless chain (2000, 0) → (2000, 800) → (2600, 1500); the three roles | refused, as above | CU whole [0] |
| a chord (0, 2000) → (4000, 2000) and a widthless chain T'd off it (2000, 2000) → (2000, 2800) → (2500, 3300); the three roles | the upper face refused; CU refused | CU whole [1, 0] |
| BU: a chord at hw 30, a cul-de-sac WAY (1000, 0) → (1000, 800) → (1500, 1400) at hw 20, wall:1 (3000, 2000) → (3000, 4000); corridorUnion at L2, then bandUnion of wall:1 at 50 cm square over the three L1 faces at L3 | CU commits 3 blocks; the L3 read of the cul-de-sac's face and bandUnion refused `RING_CROSSES` (also with the cul-de-sac straight, (1000, 700) → (1000, 1400)) | CU 3 blocks; bandUnion band 4 / blocks 4 |

The guard's `ringCrosses` returns true on two non-neighbouring ring edges collinear and overlapping — exactly F's walk
out along a dangling chain's second edge and back; for a one-edge chain the two walk edges are neighbours and are
skipped, so only chains of two or more edges are refused. Input LAWFUL (an L1 face holding a dangling chain is an arena
the kernel builds; a cul-de-sac of two segments is the commonest such chain; the band op's own B-FUZZ calls it over every
face) → N-58 verdict MAKE-IT-SUCCEED. The required change is in the verdict above.

Not blockers (appended to `checks/M0-a-09-notes.md`, rows 144 – 145; row 146 the disclosures):
